evidence: Draft judged: "I can tell when my body is saying no, before my conscious mind can twist it around to a yes." It sits once, verbatim, as the last sentence of the second paragraph in CONTEXT.txt. Compared word by word with SOURCE.txt: his published line ("I can catch the body's no before the conscious mind writes a persuasive little essay called yes.") and the replaced words ("And I can notice my body saying no before my conscious mind talks me into a yes."). It does what the_change says: Emulate's sentence as it came, with no fix by the writer (the_change names none), the body's no noticed before the conscious mind can twist it into a yes. Kept: the same actors (I, my body, my conscious mind), the same order of events (I catch the no first, the mind's override comes after) and the same outcome (a yes in place of the body's no). No claim, person, number or condition is added. Differences I checked and accept: (1) "catch the body's no" for "tell when my body is saying no" is the same detection claim, and "before" still marks that I tell before the mind acts; (2) his "writes a persuasive little essay called yes" (an override by rationalising argument, with a wry edge) becomes "twist it around to a yes", which is flatter and loses "persuasive" and "essay", but it keeps the conscious mind turning the body's no into a yes, with the same actor and outcome, the replaced words had already dropped the essay, and the change does not say it restores it, so this is a loss of colour, not of a claim; (3) "can twist" gives the mind the ability his "writes" already implies; (4) "my" for "the" matches the first-person paragraph and the replaced words; (5) the leading "And" of the replaced words is gone, a matter of style only. Linter D9 (follows the source order): accepted. One sentence replaces one sentence with the same single point, nothing is reordered, and the sentence does notice something inside it (that the mind acts after the body does), so T13 and T09 do not apply. Tell rows T01 to T29 and C01 to C04 were judged on the literal draft in its context and none is PRESENT. Looked at closely and found absent: T02 and T12 (this is the third "I can ..." statement of the paragraph, but the first two are unchanged text, the replaced words had the same shape, and they describe what he can do, they are not teaching steps); T26 ("I can tell" repeats from the sentence before, but it is a plain phrase, not a distinctive one, and the repeat is what marks the parallel abilities); T17, T20 and T08 ("to a yes" ends the paragraph, but it is a plain figure with nothing explaining it after, and the replaced words ended the same way); T15 (a recast in plainer words, not rarer words swapped in); C02 ("it" is the "no" earlier in the same sentence, and the only thing a yes can be twisted from); C03 (the claim is in his published line). Provenance note on ADMISSION.json, not on the draft: its T14 and T15 evidence says the sentence "puts back the author's own point that Emulate dropped", which is boilerplate here because the_change says nothing was put back; the ABSENT statuses still stand.
